page: Microsoft Azure D8as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dav6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Geekbench single-core and text processing scores are also strong, ranking in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, align with average tiers. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only small block at 607.87 GB/sec and large block at 39.14 GB/sec, fall within the middle 50% range. For language model workloads, the instance demonstrates strong text generation speeds of 278.01 tokens/second for small 135M models, but prompt processing for medium 7B models drops to the bottom 25% at 23.62 tokens/second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D8as_v6 offers a balanced resource profile suitable for general-purpose workloads that require strong single-threaded performance without the overhead of local storage or specialized accelerators. The absence of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled from compute resources. This configuration is suited for web serving, software compilation, database operations, and light text processing tasks where single-core execution speed is prioritized over massive multi-threaded scaling.
